merge(cpp): integration stage 3b of the native gateway: regex engine swap and two slimming branches onto stage 2b

CONTEXT (you have no other context than this prompt and the repository)
You start from branch `agent-jobs/cppgw-integrate-s2b-20261118-44298458094-1` of ubiquity/ai.ubq.fi (report `cpp/gateway/docs/findings/cppgw-integrate-s2b-20261118.md`): `cpp/gateway/` is a C++20 port of this repository's TypeScript gateway (`src/`, `serve.ts`) with a JavaScript-style runtime layer (`include/uos/rt`, `src/rt`, `src/runtime`) and vendored libraries under `cpp/gateway/third_party/`. On this state Linux ARM64 passes 448/448 release binaries and 5,086/5,086 cases. Every deployment target is 64-bit ARM.

OWNER POLICY (binding): generic functionality comes from mature open-source or standard libraries; exact parity with Bun's quirks and error wording is NOT required; less first-party code is preferred. What must hold: the gateway's functional behaviour (wire formats, status codes, stored data, authentication and validation decisions, accounting) and security never getting weaker.

READ FIRST: `cpp/gateway/docs/CI.md` (portable build-and-test driver; invoke it as `bash cpp/gateway/tools/ci-build.sh --config release --shard N/4`), `cpp/gateway/docs/BUILD.md`, `cpp/gateway/PORTING.md` (its coroutine rules are mandatory; its "Host safety" and "compile only through tools/unit.sh" rules apply to the authors' server, not to your disposable runner; where it demands exact Bun parity, the owner policy wins), and the stage 2b report.

GENERAL RULES
- The runner holds a model gateway token: never print it or write any credential to a file. Run tests with an empty `HOME`, a fresh `TMPDIR` and no provider variables. No real provider traffic: use local mocks only.
- Do not edit `.github/` (unless your task says so), the TypeScript, or `cpp/` outside `cpp/gateway/`. Do not delete or weaken tests.
- Model connections can drop: create your report file in the first minutes and commit small steps often (the tree must build at each commit). Leave no build output, binaries or downloads in the checkout.
- Report file: `cpp/gateway/docs/findings/<job id>.md`: what you did, exact commands, real counts and measurements, what is unfinished, defects found outside your paths (report, do not fix). End your final message with the same summary.

YOUR MACHINE: GitHub-hosted Linux ARM64 runner (Ubuntu 24.04, 4 CPUs, 16 GB, sudo, network). Its packages are too old for this tree: install Clang 21 or newer from apt.llvm.org (or GCC 14+), build Boost 1.92.0 `json` and `container` static libraries from the official source archive in a temp directory (the tree needs Boost >= 1.86), install OpenSSL 3, zlib, ICU, brotli, zstd development packages and build SQLite 3.54.0 as `cpp/gateway/docs/CI.md` describes. Bun 1.4.0 may be installed when you need to run the TypeScript.


OWNED PATHS
- anything under `cpp/gateway/` that the integration needs. Not `.github/`, not the TypeScript. Vendored sources under `cpp/gateway/third_party/` stay byte-identical to the branch that brings them.

TASK
Merge these three reviewed branches into your branch, in this order, each with an ordinary `git merge` commit (fetch each from origin), building and running the affected tests after each:
1. `agent-jobs/cppgw-slim-file-urls-20261118-44298551168-1` (report `cpp/gateway/docs/findings/cppgw-slim-file-urls-20261118.md`): trusted bundled-resource lookups use `std::filesystem` paths instead of file URLs. Branched from a commit your branch already contains.
2. `agent-jobs/cppgw-slim-numbers-20261118-44298517687-1` (report `cpp/gateway/docs/findings/cppgw-slim-numbers-20261118.md`): removes unused numeric helpers (`parseFloat`, radix `numberToString`, `toFixed`) and their tests. Branched from a commit your branch already contains. If your branch has gained a caller of a removed helper, replace that call with the standard library; do not restore the helper.
3. `agent-jobs/cppgw-std-regex-c2-44298488608-1` (reports `cpp/gateway/docs/findings/cppgw-std-regex-c2.md` and the earlier regex reports on that branch): replaces the hand-written regular-expression engine with the vendored quickjs-ng `libregexp` (`third_party/`), deleting about 5,400 first-party lines. It was branched from a much OLDER commit, so expect conflicts in build registration (`CMakeLists.txt`, `cmake/vendors.json`, `tools/vendor_sources.py`, `tools/links.py` data) and in documents: keep every vendored library both sides register, and for `src/rt/regex*` and `include/uos/rt/regex.hpp` take the regex branch's content. For every other file take your branch's content unless the regex branch changed it on purpose for the engine swap.
That regex branch's own full sweep had exactly two failing test binaries, both stored-value (KV) differential tests that assert the retired engine's diagnostic wording or missing `v`-flag support. Find them (its report names them), and fix the EXPECTATIONS so they assert the new engine's behaviour: the gateway decision each case covers (accept or reject, stored bytes, status code) must stay asserted; only quirk wording and the engine capability may change. Record each changed expectation, before and after, in your report. Add an entry to `cpp/gateway/docs/DEVIATIONS-FROM-BUN.md` for anything user-visible.
Also: stage 2b capped JSON and stored-graph nesting depth; make sure the regex branch does not undo it. Do not delete or weaken any other test. If a merged branch conflicts with stage 2b's behaviour, stage 2b wins unless the branch's report says the change is its purpose.

DONE WHEN
All three merges are in; all four release shards pass every binary and case on your Linux ARM64 runner (state the totals; expected at least 448 binaries); the sanitizer configuration (`--config asan`) passes for the regex, KV, URL, static-file, number and permissions tests at minimum; `python3 cpp/gateway/tools/links.py --check` passes; the report lists each merge's conflicts and resolutions, the changed expectations, first-party production line counts before and after, and anything unfinished.
